items.question: What is object orientation? What are the three rules to remember?
items.answer: Answer: Python is an object-oriented programming language, and so are C++ and Java. The three rules are: (1) the world is a collection of objects, so look at everything as an object; (2) every object belongs to a type, the type is called a class, the class is imaginary and the object is real; (3) every object has a has-part and a does-part. The has-part is coded with variables (data types), and the does-part is coded with methods or functions.

items.question: Where should you type a Python program? Can you use Paint, Word or a media player?
items.answer: Answer: No. Python code has to be typed in a code editor, not in software such as Paint, Microsoft Word (a documentation software) or a music or video player like VLC. The simplest code editor already in the computer is Notepad, and VS Code is a well-known code editor.

items.question: Write and explain the first Python program.
items.answer: Answer: The program prints a message. print is written in small letters, followed by simple parentheses, and the message to print is written within double quotes. There is no semicolon, no public static void main as in Java, and no #include as in C and C++; Python needs only the print statement. print("Hello, students") Output: Hello, students

items.question: What is the difference between RAM and the hard disk? Why must the program be saved?
items.answer: Answer: Whatever you type goes first into the RAM, which is a volatile memory device: the data stays only while it is getting electricity, and when the electricity goes, everything typed is gone. The hard disk is a non-volatile (permanent) memory device: the data stays even when the computer is shut down and switched on again, which is why movies, photos and files stay. To make the program permanent, you must save it, which stores it in the hard disk. The C drive and the D drive are compartments of the hard disk.

items.question: How do you save a Python file in Notepad, and why is the .py extension compulsory?
items.answer: Answer: Create a folder in a drive (for example D drive, because the C drive is meant for the operating system), go to File > Save As, open that folder, give the file a name such as hello.py, and change Save as type from text document to All files. The computer understands which kind of code the file holds from its extension, so .py is compulsory; if it is missing, the program will not execute and the file will not get the Python icon. .c C code .cpp C++ code .java Java code .js JavaScript code .html HTML code .css CSS code .ipynb Python notebook .py Python code

items.question: What is the operating system, and what is the command prompt?
items.answer: Answer: The operating system is the boss of the computer, which monitors and operates the whole system. A computer does not allow you to talk to the operating system directly; you talk to it through the command prompt. Analogy: you cannot directly meet the CEO of a company; you first go through the reception and the CEO's personal assistant. The command prompt is that personal assistant: it is called a prompt because you give it messages, and the messages are given as commands. Open it by searching for cmd.

items.question: How do you check whether Python is installed and which version it is?
items.answer: Answer: In the command prompt, type python --version and press enter. If Python is installed, the version is displayed (for example Python 3.14). If it is not installed, or the operating system cannot find it, the message "python is not recognized as an internal or external command" appears. Python 1 and Python 2 are outdated and should never be used; use Python 3 (3.13 is fine, and 3.14 is also fine, for example for machine learning). python --version

items.question: Which command prompt commands are used to reach the program file?
items.answer: Answer: Type the drive letter followed by a colon to switch the drive (d:). dir lists the folders and files of the current location, cd (change directory) enters a folder, cd .. goes one step back, and cls (clear screen) clears the screen. In the class, the folder was created on the D drive, so the steps were d:, dir, cd first, dir (which shows hello.py). Type the folder name exactly as it appears, with the same capital and small letters. d: dir cd first dir cd .. cls

items.question: How do you run the Python program from the command prompt?
items.answer: Answer: Go to the folder that contains the file and type python followed by the file name. You do not compile separately (unlike javac in Java), because compilation happens internally and automatically. python hello.py Output: Hello, students

items.question: Why can't the high-level Python program be given directly to the microprocessor?
items.answer: Answer: The program is written in a high-level language (print, brackets, words). The microprocessor understands only machine-level language, that is zeros and ones. So the program must be translated before it is executed.

items.question: What is the execution flow of a Python program?
items.answer: Answer: The Python code (hello.py) is first converted by the Python compiler into bytecode. The bytecode cannot go to the microprocessor directly, because it is not pure machine level language. The PVM (Python Virtual Machine) takes the bytecode, and the interpreter inside the PVM converts it to machine-level language line by line and gives it to the microprocessor, which gives the output. Compilation to bytecode happens automatically and internally, and you invoke the PVM by typing python in the command prompt. Python code (.py) -> Python compiler -> bytecode -> PVM (interpreter) -> machine level language -> microprocessor -> output

items.question: Is Python a compiled or an interpreted language?
items.answer: Answer: Python is a hybrid language: it uses both compilation and interpretation. The code is compiled to bytecode automatically, and the interpreter inside the PVM then executes the bytecode line by line. Many textbooks and people call Python an interpreted language because the developer never does the compilation by hand, so the compilation step is hidden. In an interview, the best answer is that Python is compiled as well as interpreted, and you can explain the process on paper up to the bytecode.

items.question: How is the execution of Python different from Java?
items.answer: Answer: The process is similar in both languages: source code, compiler, bytecode, virtual machine. In Java, the developer must compile explicitly (javac Hello.java) to get the bytecode and then give it to the JVM. In Python, the compilation is automatic, so the developer only asks the PVM to execute the program (python hello.py). javac Hello.java // Java: compile explicitly java Hello // Java: JVM executes the bytecode python hello.py // Python: compilation is automatic, PVM executes

items.question: What is an IDE, and which tools are available for Python?
items.answer: Answer: An IDE (Integrated Development Environment) or code editor is software built to type and run code easily. Notepad is not used for Python coding: it has no colours for text, brackets and functions, so the code is hard to read, and everything has to be typed. The tools mentioned are IDLE, VS Code, PyCharm, Jupyter Notebook, Google Colab, Spyder and Cursor (an AI-powered IDE). All of them run the program through the same internal process.

items.question: What is IDLE, and what is its Shell?
items.answer: Answer: IDLE is the beginner-friendly IDE that comes automatically when Python is installed; search for IDLE to open it. Its window is called the Shell. In the Shell you type one line, press enter, and the output of that line comes immediately, because the interpreter executes line by line. If there is a mistake, it reports it immediately, for example an unclosed string gives a SyntaxError, which must be fixed before you proceed. >>> print("Hello, students") Hello, students >>> print(100 + 200) 300 >>> print("Hello SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line 1)

items.question: How do you write and run a complete program in IDLE?
items.answer: Answer: The Shell executes one line at a time, so to type a complete program first and run it later, create a file: File > New File, type the instructions, then Run > Run Module (shortcut F5). If the file is not saved, IDLE asks you to save it; save it in your folder with a name such as hello2.py, and then the output of the whole file appears in the Shell. The advantage over Notepad is that everything happens inside the tool, and you do not have to go to the command prompt each time.

items.question: Which IDE is recommended for which purpose?
items.answer: Answer: IDLE is only for a beginner, to see how each line executes. For web development, automation and general Python development, VS Code and PyCharm are the best. For machine learning, deep learning, data analytics and data visualization, Jupyter Notebook, Google Colab and Spyder are used. Cursor is an AI IDE, where you give a prompt and it types the code. VS Code is the most used (the instructor quoted about 45 to 48 percent of Python developers, with PyCharm around 25 percent), and it is free and open source; PyCharm's support for web frameworks such as Django is in its paid edition. VS Code was the editor chosen for the course, and Notepad is never used.

items.question: What features of Python were mentioned?
items.answer: Answer: Simple and readable, platform independent, object oriented, dynamically typed, interpreted (together with compilation, as explained above), huge library, high performance, multithreaded and distributed. Platform independence and object orientation were taught in the earlier classes.
